verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents programmatic machine management. Machines can be created through the API or CLI, and the HTTP API is described as a way to "programmatically manage Paperspace resources." A creation-time starting state and an auto-shutdown that puts idle machines into a stop state are also documented, and a user reports paying an hourly rate for GPU VMs. However, none of the evidence names explicit start, stop, restart or terminate operations, and stop-state billing semantics are never stated. missing for 10: explicitly documented start/stop/restart/delete API or CLI operations, documented billing behavior for stopped vs running machines, hands-on corroboration of programmatic lifecycle control.

support.subject: As a developer, I can start, stop, restart, and terminate instances programmatically and keep paying only for what is running

citations.quote: You can create a Linux machine using the Paperspace console, Paperspace API, or Paperspace CLI.
Programmatically manage Paperspace resources using conventional HTTP requests.
Programmatically manage resources using the Paperspace Command Line Interface.
The auto-shutdown feature places your machine in a stop state after a predefined period of inactivity
When you create a new machine, you choose your machine type, operating system or custom template, disk size, region, authentication, starting state
An hourly rate on a standard VM w/GPU is better than buying a local machine
